comments.note: nodes.py uses a module-level _MISSING sentinel (line ~155) for the getter nodes. The LoadJsonNode does not need this pattern, but its absence from the load path is consistent — no issues found in the touched code.

The placeholder [''] emitted by define_schema when no .json files exist results in an empty string being passed to execute()/fingerprint_inputs(). Both methods call os.path.realpath(os.path.join(input_dir, '')) which resolves to input_dir itself, so the path-traversal guard fires ('candidate == real_input' is True for fingerprint but False for the startswith check). Consider adding an explicit early guard in execute() for filename == '' to give a clearer error message rather than a path-traversal rejection, but this is a low-priority UX improvement only triggered when the input directory has no .json files.

summary: Reviewed 2 files (nodes.py, __init__.py). All OWASP Top 10 categories audited. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium findings. 2 Low/Info observations recorded. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: A04 — Insecure Design (Low): nodes.py LoadJsonNode.execute() uses fh.read() with no file-size cap. A malicious or accidentally very large JSON file in the input directory could cause excessive memory allocation. Exploitability is minimal in a local desktop tool where only the local user controls input files, but a size guard (e.g., os.path.getsize() check before open()) would provide defense-in-depth. Recommended remediation: add an optional size check before reading, e.g. if os.path.getsize(candidate) > MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES: raise ValueError(...).

A01 — Info: fingerprint_inputs() (nodes.py ~line 901) passes the path-traversal guard when filename == '' because candidate resolves to real_input itself (candidate == real_input branch). It then returns str(os.path.getmtime(input_dir)) — the mtime of the input directory. This is not a security bypass: execute() with filename == '' will ultimately raise a ValueError via the OSError path (PermissionError on Windows when opening a directory). No exploitable vector; recorded for completeness.

No other security findings. The path-traversal guard in both execute() and fingerprint_inputs() uses os.path.realpath() with the startswith(real_input + os.sep) pattern, correctly blocking relative (../../) and absolute-path injection, and symlink traversal. json.loads() is safe (no code execution). No external dependencies introduced. All OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed — no Critical or High issues identified.
